Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus, delayed re-challenge (priming assay)
ideas.description: Expose cells to a brief stimulus (e.g., TPA, TNF, or wounding), wait days to weeks after FOS/JUN levels return to baseline, then re-stimulate and compare transcriptional output (RNA-seq) against naive cells. Like the material's 'ledger' that remembers the marble, the readout is a stored record that changes later responses. Include AP-1 inhibitors (e.g., T-5224) or dominant-negative FOS (A-FOS) present only during the first stimulus to test whether AP-1 is needed to establish the memory.

ideas.title: Longitudinal chromatin accessibility and AP-1 footprinting
ideas.description: Run ATAC-seq or CUT&Tag for AP-1 factors and H3K27ac at time points before, during and long after the stimulus. Check whether AP-1 motif-containing enhancers stay open after the AP-1 proteins have left, and whether they are the same loci that show the primed response. The 'braided ribbon' pattern is an interleaving of AP-1 binding with other pioneer or chromatin factors that keep sites open.

ideas.title: Single-cell live imaging of AP-1 dynamics with history
ideas.description: Use endogenously tagged FOS/JUN or AP-1 reporters in single cells, delivering pulses of different number and spacing. Test whether past pulses change later response amplitude (hysteresis) and whether the response is cell-autonomous and inherited by daughter cells after division. The 'rehearsing kite' idea: repeated practice changes later performance, which can be measured as a function of history.

ideas.title: Targeted perturbation of memory-specific enhancers
ideas.description: Use CRISPRi/dCas9 or motif mutation at candidate AP-1-dependent enhancers only after the initial stimulus, and optionally use acute degron tags (dTAG) to remove AP-1 at defined times. If memory is maintained by AP-1 continuously, late depletion should erase it. If AP-1 only writes memory, late depletion should not. This separates initiation from maintenance, like the 'hinge' that must be present to set a position but not to hold it.

ideas.title: Mathematical modeling and bistability tests
ideas.description: Build a model of AP-1 feedback (e.g., JUN autoregulation, with chromatin states) and fit it to dose-response and washout data. Test its predictions: bistability, a threshold dose for memory, and a hysteresis loop, with experiments such as dose titration and cell-sorting by AP-1 level. A 'lattice weighing its feather' suggests looking for a small stimulus change that tips a network between stable states.
